hero.eyebrow: Cyber Security at Riphah · Web pentesting · CTF
hero.description: I’m Muhammad Abdullah, also known online as Abdullah Cyber—a Cyber Security student at Riphah International University in Pakistan, focused on web penetration testing, practical labs and CTF challenges.

about.lead: I focus on web penetration testing—understanding how applications behave, questioning their trust boundaries and finding weaknesses before attackers do.
paragraphs: As a Bachelor of Cyber Security student at Riphah International University, I am building practical experience in Pakistan through authorized assessments, security labs, internships and CTF events.

My learning is practical: I combine Linux, networking and Docker fundamentals with vulnerability testing, security controls and CTF problem-solving. I am continuously improving through labs, projects and collaborative security events.
about.quote: Security is not only about tools. It starts with understanding what an application assumes—and what happens when those assumptions break.
about.contextTitle: Cyber Security student at Riphah International University
about.contextText: Muhammad Abdullah’s portfolio documents practical web security learning in Pakistan, including penetration-testing internships, authorized phishing-awareness work, an SSH honeypot lab and competitive CTF experience.

projects.title: Authorized Phishing Awareness Campaign
projects.description: Designed and conducted an authorized Gophish simulation to assess real-world phishing awareness among students in a controlled academic setting.

caseStudy.label: Case study / Social engineering
caseStudy.summary: A controlled, academically supervised simulation designed to evaluate how users respond to realistic phishing cues without exposing participants to harmful content.
caseStudy.objective: Assess awareness, observe interaction patterns and identify opportunities for better security education.
caseStudy.environment: Gophish-based campaign conducted under academic supervision with an explicitly authorized scope.
caseStudy.learning: Campaign configuration, ethical scoping, communication design, result interpretation and awareness-focused reporting.
caseStudy.ethics: No unauthorized targeting. The activity was conducted as a supervised learning exercise with a defined audience and purpose.

projects.title: SSH Honeypot Deployment
projects.description: Deployed an SSH honeypot using sshesame inside VirtualBox to observe brute-force behavior and study attacker interaction patterns.

caseStudy.label: Case study / Threat observation
caseStudy.summary: A lab deployment created to expose a controlled SSH service and study automated brute-force behavior in an isolated environment.
caseStudy.objective: Observe login attempts, attacker patterns and the value of deception systems for security learning.
caseStudy.environment: sshesame deployed inside a VirtualBox lab with controlled networking and logging.
caseStudy.learning: Linux services, SSH behavior, log review, safe exposure design and basic attacker-behavior analysis.
caseStudy.ethics: Isolated lab setup with no offensive interaction against external systems.
